questionText: [Set 36.1] In wetland puddle rice (paddy) cultivation, maintaining a continuous shallow standing water depth of 2 to 5 cm during the critical tillering stage is beneficial because it:

options.text: Accelerates soil erosion and nutrient leaching
Eliminates the need for nitrogen fertilizers completely
Suppresses weed germination and maintains uniform soil microclimate
Induces floral sterility and fungal blight

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agronomy of Major Cereal Crops - Rice Cultivation Water Management):
Puddling and maintaining a 2-5 cm water layer in rice fields creates anaerobic conditions that suppress weed seed germination and reduce deep percolation, conserving soil moisture during vegetative tillering.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Agronomy of Major Cereal Crops: Rice Cultivation Water Management
solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agronomy of Major Cereal Crops - Rice Cultivation Water Management):
Puddling and maintaining a 2-5 cm water layer in rice fields creates anaerobic conditions that suppress weed seed germination and reduce deep percolation, conserving soil moisture during vegetative tillering.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

keyConcept: Agronomy of Major Cereal Crops: Rice Cultivation Water Management

questionText: [Set 36.2] In agricultural emissions, anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in flooded paddy soils and enteric fermentation in ruminant livestock are major sources of:

options.text: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
Methane (CH_4)
Sulfur hexafluoride (SF_6)
Lead tetraethyl vapors

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agrometeorology and Climate Change - Greenhouse Gases in Agriculture: Methane):
Methanogenic archaea in the anaerobic zone of flooded rice paddies and the rumen of cattle decompose cellulose, releasing methane ($CH_4$), a potent greenhouse gas with 28 times the global warming potential of $CO_2$.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agrometeorology and Climate Change - Greenhouse Gases in Agriculture: Methane):
Methanogenic archaea in the anaerobic zone of flooded rice paddies and the rumen of cattle decompose cellulose, releasing methane ($CH_4$), a potent greenhouse gas with 28 times the global warming potential of $CO_2$.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.3] In plant breeding, 'Heterosis' or hybrid vigour refers to the genetic phenomenon where:

options.text: The F_1 hybrid offspring exhibits superior phenotypic performance, yield, and vigor compared to both inbred parental lines
Continuous self-pollination leads to progressive reduction in biological fitness
A diploid plant spontaneously doubles its chromosome number into a tetraploid
A mutated recessive gene completely replaces all dominant alleles in the genome

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Genetics and Plant Breeding - Heterosis (Hybrid Vigour) Exploitation):
Heterosis is the phenotypic superiority of heterozygous $F_1$ hybrids over both homozygous inbred parents with respect to biomass, grain yield, disease resistance, and environmental stress tolerance.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Genetics and Plant Breeding: Heterosis (Hybrid Vigour) Exploitation
solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Genetics and Plant Breeding - Heterosis (Hybrid Vigour) Exploitation):
Heterosis is the phenotypic superiority of heterozygous $F_1$ hybrids over both homozygous inbred parents with respect to biomass, grain yield, disease resistance, and environmental stress tolerance.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

keyConcept: Genetics and Plant Breeding: Heterosis (Hybrid Vigour) Exploitation

questionText: [Set 36.4] In legume root nodules, the red/pink pigment 'Leghemoglobin' plays an indispensable biological role by:

options.text: Synthesizing starch polymers from atmospheric carbon dioxide
Absorbing blue light photons for root photosynthesis
Transporting nitrogen gas directly into the phloem vessels
Scavenging oxygen to protect the oxygen-sensitive Nitrogenase enzyme while providing oxygen for bacterial respiration

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Biochemistry and Microbiology - Rhizobium-Legume Symbiotic Nitrogen Fixation):
Nitrogenase, the enzyme catalyzing $N_2$ reduction to $NH_3$, is irreversibly inactivated by molecular oxygen. Leghemoglobin acts as an oxygen buffer, maintaining low free $O_2$ levels while delivering sufficient $O_2$ for bacteroid cellular respiration.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Biochemistry and Microbiology: Rhizobium-Legume Symbiotic Nitrogen Fixation

Detailed Solution:

questionText: [Set 36.5] Which of the following indigenous zebu cattle breeds (Bos indicus) is recognized as the highest milk-producing dairy breed in India?

options.text: Sahiwal (originating from Montgomery district)
Amritmahal
Kangayam
Hallikar

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:

Sahiwal (native to the dry Punjab-Montgomery region) is the premier indigenous dairy breed of India, known for high milk yield (2,000-2,500 kg per lactation), high butterfat content (4.5-5%), and tick resistance.

questionText: [Set 36.6] In horticultural fruit propagation, 'Air Layering' (Gootee) is commonly employed for commercial multiplication of:

options.text: Wheat and Barley
Pomegranate, Guava, and Litchi
Mustard and Sunflower
Sugarcane and Maize

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Horticulture - Air Layering (Gootee) Vegetative Propagation):
Air layering (Gootee) involves girdling a healthy pencil-thick shoot, applying rooting hormone (IBA), and wrapping with moist sphagnum moss and polythene to induce adventitious roots while still attached to the parent plant.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.7] In animal nutrition, 'Total Digestible Nutrients' (TDN) measures the energy value of a feedstuff calculated as:

options.text: Digestible Crude Protein / Total Ash Content
Digestible Crude Protein + Digestible Crude Fiber + Digestible Nitrogen-Free Extract + (2.25 * Digestible Crude Fat)
Total Moisture Content + Crude Fiber Percentage
Net Mineral Energy * Dry Matter Percentage

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Animal Nutrition and Feed Technology - Total Digestible Nutrients (TDN) Concept):
TDN represents the sum of all digestible organic nutrients. Because fat yields 2.25 times as much energy as carbohydrates upon oxidation, digestible ether extract (fat) is multiplied by 2.25.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.8] Millets (such as Pearl Millet/Bajra, Finger Millet/Ragi, and Sorghum/Jowar) are designated as 'Nutri-Cereals' because they are exceptionally rich in:

options.text: Gluten proteins suitable for leavened bakery bread
Refined simple sucrose sugars and saturated animal fats
Dietary fiber, iron, calcium (especially Ragi), and essential micronutrients with a low glycemic index
Pure starch devoid of any minerals or vitamins

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agronomy of Millets, Pulses and Oilseeds - International Year of Millets: Nutritional Superiority):
Millets are climate-resilient C4 crops rich in calcium (Ragi has ~344 mg/100g, 30x higher than rice), iron, dietary fiber, and antioxidants, and are gluten-free with low glycemic index.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.25] In wetland puddle rice (paddy) cultivation, maintaining a continuous shallow standing water depth of 2 to 5 cm during the critical tillering stage is beneficial because it:

options.text: Accelerates soil erosion and nutrient leaching
Eliminates the need for nitrogen fertilizers completely
Suppresses weed germination and maintains uniform soil microclimate
Induces floral sterility and fungal blight

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.28] In legume root nodules, the red/pink pigment 'Leghemoglobin' plays an indispensable biological role by:

options.text: Synthesizing starch polymers from atmospheric carbon dioxide
Absorbing blue light photons for root photosynthesis
Transporting nitrogen gas directly into the phloem vessels
Scavenging oxygen to protect the oxygen-sensitive Nitrogenase enzyme while providing oxygen for bacterial respiration

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Biochemistry and Microbiology - Rhizobium-Legume Symbiotic Nitrogen Fixation):
Nitrogenase, the enzyme catalyzing $N_2$ reduction to $NH_3$, is irreversibly inactivated by molecular oxygen. Leghemoglobin acts as an oxygen buffer, maintaining low free $O_2$ levels while delivering sufficient $O_2$ for bacteroid cellular respiration.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.47] In animal nutrition, 'Total Digestible Nutrients' (TDN) measures the energy value of a feedstuff calculated as:

options.text: Digestible Crude Protein + Digestible Crude Fiber + Digestible Nitrogen-Free Extract + (2.25 * Digestible Crude Fat)
Digestible Crude Protein / Total Ash Content
Total Moisture Content + Crude Fiber Percentage
Net Mineral Energy * Dry Matter Percentage

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Animal Nutrition and Feed Technology - Total Digestible Nutrients (TDN) Concept):
TDN represents the sum of all digestible organic nutrients. Because fat yields 2.25 times as much energy as carbohydrates upon oxidation, digestible ether extract (fat) is multiplied by 2.25.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.48] Millets (such as Pearl Millet/Bajra, Finger Millet/Ragi, and Sorghum/Jowar) are designated as 'Nutri-Cereals' because they are exceptionally rich in:

options.text: Gluten proteins suitable for leavened bakery bread
Refined simple sucrose sugars and saturated animal fats
Dietary fiber, iron, calcium (especially Ragi), and essential micronutrients with a low glycemic index
Pure starch devoid of any minerals or vitamins

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agronomy of Millets, Pulses and Oilseeds - International Year of Millets: Nutritional Superiority):
Millets are climate-resilient C4 crops rich in calcium (Ragi has ~344 mg/100g, 30x higher than rice), iron, dietary fiber, and antioxidants, and are gluten-free with low glycemic index.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.49] In wetland puddle rice (paddy) cultivation, maintaining a continuous shallow standing water depth of 2 to 5 cm during the critical tillering stage is beneficial because it:

options.text: Suppresses weed germination and maintains uniform soil microclimate
Accelerates soil erosion and nutrient leaching
Eliminates the need for nitrogen fertilizers completely
Induces floral sterility and fungal blight

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agronomy of Major Cereal Crops - Rice Cultivation Water Management):
Puddling and maintaining a 2-5 cm water layer in rice fields creates anaerobic conditions that suppress weed seed germination and reduce deep percolation, conserving soil moisture during vegetative tillering.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 36.50] In agricultural emissions, anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in flooded paddy soils and enteric fermentation in ruminant livestock are major sources of:

options.text: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
Sulfur hexafluoride (SF_6)
Methane (CH_4)
Lead tetraethyl vapors

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Agriculture (Agrometeorology and Climate Change - Greenhouse Gases in Agriculture: Methane):
Methanogenic archaea in the anaerobic zone of flooded rice paddies and the rumen of cattle decompose cellulose, releasing methane ($CH_4$), a potent greenhouse gas with 28 times the global warming potential of $CO_2$.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.
